A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TAR3D, with matching architecture, equations and retained experiments. All text, tables, figures and supplementary material support comparison. v1 has no separate appendix; v2 includes supplementary Sections A–B.

before.justification: Sections 4.2–4.4 report original image-to-3D and text-to-3D outputs, quantitative benchmark results and component ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds GSO qualitative evaluations and a triplane-size ablation reporting reconstruction quality and inference time.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain the same triplane VQ-VAE, plane-interaction decoder, sequence ordering, TriPE, autoregressive generator and losses. The guidance-scale revision is an experimental setting change; the new SyncMVD attribution documents the unchanged Figure 1.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained ShapeNet and Objaverse coverage, v2 adds out-of-domain image-to-3D evaluation on real-world GSO scans, demonstrated in Figures 4 and 9. This introduces a distinct generalization scenario. ABO and OmniObject3D are only proposed for future work.

E2.justification: v2 adds LGM to Table 1. The replacement image-to-3D Figure 4 adds LGM and LN3Diff and omits Shap-E, which remains in Table 1 and the text-to-3D comparison. OpenLRM is named in prose but has no identifiable displayed result, so its participation cannot be verified.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported filtered Objaverse pool from about 210,000 to 100,000 objects, the F-score threshold from 0.2 to 0.02, and CFG scale from 5 to 7.5. v2 also introduces evaluation across three triplane sizes with inference timing. These materially revise stated settings, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The VAE/VQ-VAE, plane-interaction and TriPE ablations are retained. v2 adds triplane-size sensitivity covering geometry quality and inference speed (Table 4 and Figure 7), plus GSO distribution-shift evidence (Figures 4 and 9), substantially broadening the questions examined.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, error bars, confidence intervals or formal significance tests for its experiments. Results remain point estimates.

E6.justification: Existing values in Tables 1–3 remain unchanged. v2 adds LGM scores, including Chamfer distance 0.149 and F-score 0.172. Table 4 adds Chamfer distances 0.157/0.066/0.062 and times 17.7/67.6/143.9 seconds for increasing triplane sizes. New GSO outputs and replacement Figure 4 cases broaden the findings; they do not demonstrate a same-setting performance gain over v1.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6), quantization definitions, autoregressive factorization, TriPE construction and loss mathematics are unchanged. The supplement introduces no new formal assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: fixed-length triplane quantization, autoregressive part generation, PII and TriPE, and superior conditional-generation quality. References to additional datasets broaden supporting evidence without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explains the default triplane size as a quality–speed tradeoff. It replaces v1's approximately 10% VQ-VAE superiority discussion with disclosure of tuning until performance matches or exceeds the VAE. Supplementary Sections A–B add concrete qualifications about poor ULIP renderings, noisy captions and remaining sequence inefficiency.

D1.justification: Figure 1 newly credits SyncMVD for texture synthesis, and the project-page link is replaced by a repository link. Experimental settings are revised, but v2 removes the explicit ShapeNet-chair scope of the original ablations and the TriPE figure's 20-degree rendering elevation. Most architecture, optimizer and hardware details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds AutoSDF as an autoregressive 3D antecedent and citations for OpenLRM, GSO, SyncMVD, Cap3D, ABO and OmniObject3D. Several citations are removed, including VAR and Lumina-mGPT. The central positioning against diffusion and mesh-face autoregression remains intact; LGM and LN3Diff were already cited in v1.

P1.justification: The introduction is refocused from general multimodal/AGI motivation toward fixed-length mesh tokenization, with targeted edits to related work and ablation explanations. v2 adds supplementary visualization and discussion sections, while retaining the main section sequence and nearly identical methodology prose.

P2.justification: v2 replaces Figure 4, adds Table 4 and Figures 7 and 9, and transposes Tables 2–3 into a compact arrangement beside Table 4. The original galleries in v1 Figures 5 and 7 move to supplementary Figures 8 and 10. The retained text comparison and TriPE visualization are also relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The added GSO evidence and quality–latency ablation strengthen generalization support and justify the default triplane size. Explicit data-quality limitations and SyncMVD attribution improve transparency. These gains are limited by removed ablation details and unexplained setting revisions accompanying unchanged numerical results, which leave uncertainty about how the retained experiments relate to the revised protocol.
